To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the EMT spectrum in cancer cells is a key player in shaping the TME, which in turn influences the immune response and the efficacy of immunotherapy.

cancer cells undergoing EMT or oscillating within this spectrum may escape the antitumor immune response by several mechanisms, including the modulation of the TME, decreased susceptibility to immune cells and the induction of immune cell exhaustion.

the EMT process in tumor cells is associated with the development of an immunosuppressive microenvironment that promotes tumor growth and metastasis, and the EMT process may contribute to the resistance of cancer cells to immune therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of immune escape in cancer, the development of immunotherapy and the use of immunotherapeutics to treat cancer.
understanding how cancer cell clones with a mesenchymal phenotype could escape immune attacks.
the development of a new approach to the development of the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cancer cells undergoing EMT are not necessarily resistant to immunotherapy, but that the TME may be shaped by these cells to favor their survival, and that this may be a mechanism of resistance to immunotherapy.
cancer cells undergoing EMT are more resistant to the immune system and that targeting these cells may help overcome this resistance.
EMT is an important contributor to tumor progression, metastasis, immune escape, and drug resistance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
EMT is a dynamic process and a source of cellular heterogeneity within the tumor.
EMT is an important mechanism that cancer cells use to avoid immune recognition and destruction.
EMT is a key process in tumor immune evasion and resistance to cancer immunotherapy, and that targeting EMT could be beneficial for the efficacy of immunotherapies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cancer cell plasticity is a key feature of tumor heterogeneity that needs to be considered when designing new immunotherapeutic strategies.
EMT‐related mechanisms may play a critical role in shaping the TME, and thus, in the outcome of immunotherapies.
EMT is a key process in shaping the TME and that it may be involved in the development of resistance to immune checkpoint blockade.
